payload.pattern: A detector bound that was never sized against a real specimen is a confident GREEN over the exact thing it was built to catch
payload.solution: studio-ops scan-secrets.mjs had a HIGH-confidence Supabase Service Role rule requiring a JWT payload of {100,} characters. A self-hosted Supabase key omits the cloud-only ref claim: real payloads measure 88 (anon) and 99 (service_role). The full RLS-bypass credential missed the detector BY ONE CHARACTER, and a git-tracked file holding SERVICE_ROLE_KEY + JWT_SECRET + POSTGRES_PASSWORD was reported clean for five months while the same scanner emitted [low] noise on npm lockfile integrity hashes. Fix: make detection STRUCTURAL — match the JWT shape, decode header+payload, and let the claims set name and severity — never a length proxy. Two further lessons. (1) The FIRST test for any new matcher must fire it at a real specimen, plus a test asserting the PRE-FIX version misses that specimen, so the fixture cannot quietly stop reproducing the defect. (2) A second sweep (the infra-debt audit) had already found the same file and graded it stale-scripts — right file, wrong axis. Two instruments agreeing is not corroboration when they measure different things. Related: a module that scans-and-exits on import cannot be unit-tested, which is why this rule was never exercised at all — add a CLI main-guard.

payload.headline: A detector whose bound was never sized against a real specimen is a confident GREEN over the thing it was built to catch
lessons: A high-confidence credential rule required a JWT payload of {100,} characters. Self-hosted Supabase keys omit the cloud-only ref claim and measure 88 (anon) / 99 (service_role), so a full RLS-bypass key missed the detector BY ONE CHARACTER and a tracked file holding it was reported clean for five months. Make detection STRUCTURAL — decode and classify by claims — never a length proxy, and make the FIRST test for any matcher fire it at a real specimen plus assert the pre-fix version misses it.

A workflow that calls itself nightly is making a claim nothing checks. Removing schedule: from 55 workflows for cost was correct and silently converted a data-protection lane into a no-op: the only live cloud Supabase database went eight weeks unbacked while the file still said nightly. Two probes each reported an honest half (no lane / 14 failures) and nothing joined them to the conclusion.

A byte digest that crosses a host boundary is platform-dependent. A Linux lane writing LF and a Windows checkout reading CRLF produced two hashes for identical source, so three artifacts were permanently red and whoever ran last reddened the other. Normalize text before hashing; keep binary raw.

When a checker offers --fix, ask what the red is CARRYING before clearing it. Four stale sibling locks were the only remaining evidence that three sessions ended without closeout; the documented remedy would have deleted that signal and unblocked nothing.

A classifier with N-1 states maps the missing one onto a worse neighbour — and I rebuilt that bug inside the probe written in its spirit, grading a lane inert while its own receipt showed a success an hour earlier. Check a counter-example you know the answer to before believing your own output.

payload.pattern: A founder blocker is a claim about the secrets gateway, and a carry is not a re-check. StatVault carried [S295.H1] five sessions as needs credentials not in the gateway while check-secrets reported the capability READY the whole time; nobody re-ran the check because the premise arrived already written.
payload.solution: Before keeping ANY Human Action Required item at closeout, re-run check-secrets --for <capability> and paste the line into the carry. CANON-019: READY means agent work — provision through a gateway-backed repo script (env over ssh STDIN never argv, units from the promoted tree, one synchronous run, receipt read back). Also: measure the target on the box (container name, db user) before trusting a script written against a guess.

payload.pattern: An identity gate must be two-sided, and internal validation is not identity. A shared year guard accepted a namesake whose career began within six years of the rookie year and ran a decade past the known span; the season-sum check then proved the grid was self-consistent — for someone else. Five contaminated profiles reached main before the coherence gate ran.
payload.solution: Require a candidate span to sit INSIDE the known span (±1 year of slack), not merely to start near it; reject-prove on the live contaminations AND the genuine fills from the same pass; run the coherence gate BEFORE the commit, not after the push; and never run a widening-only repair after a backfill — it legitimizes the contamination.
